chunks: From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-'Utariq, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I buy food, and its price changes before I take possession of it.' He said: 'I like that you fulfill it for him, just as if there were a surplus in it, you would take it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling food when the price changes before taking possession?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on *bay' al-madmun* (sale of guaranteed goods) where price fluctuation occurs before physical possession (*qabd*). He encourages the buyer to fulfill the contract at the agreed price, noting that if the price has risen, the buyer benefits from the gain, but if it has fallen, the seller retains the right to the original value, thereby ensuring equity and preventing dispute in market transactions.
